title: Define settlement correction, reversal uniqueness, and control-account projections
description:
References: §§5.6/5.7, 8.1/8.2, Appendix A/B/F (lines 419-423, 519-522, 536, 1165, 1241-1246, 1335, 1339).
Open amount = original minus summed SETTLES, but no immutable application-undo law is specified when a receipt or invoice is reversed/replaced. Reversing a settled receipt's GL legs leaves the invoice closed unless settlement effects reverse too; copying the original settles into the reversal can double-apply. Define versioned application effects and their bitemporal fold, target-side/unit validation, and over-application protection.
Acyclic SUPERSEDES plus exact target negation does not prevent two different idempotency keys from reversing/replacing one original twice. O + (-O) + (-O) is still acyclic and each reversal satisfies the local rule. Specify which reversal/replacement lifecycle actions are permitted and the concurrency witness; reversing a reversal must remain explicit if supported.
§5.6 says native detail postings inherently fold into the control account. The Register key schema has one account_ref, while only Leaf accounts accept legs. Define summary roll-up ownership, prohibit double counting and specify the externally fed detail-vs-summary representation so there is no second posting universe.
Acceptance: receipt applied then reversed; invoice replaced after partial application; concurrent duplicate reversals; two customers under an AR control account plus external-summary import. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.7 application effects versioned (open = original - SETTLES + UNSETTLES; reversals carry kernel-emitted unsettles; replacements re-declare, never copy); §8.2 reversal/replacement uniqueness by identity-derived vids (second reversal = AlreadyLive conflict; reversing a reversal explicit); §5.6 leaf-only register cells with rollup cells for summaries and external detail outside the book. FA-INV-08 clauses unsettle, reversed-once. Left open for re-review.

title: Resolve round-1 architecture audit blockers before freezing G0
description:
Review of baseline ac4587c on 2026-10-09. Read the entire local AGENTS.md, suite AGENTS.md, README.md, comprehensive plan (all 1410 lines), scaffolding, and relevant live foundation source/manifests. This is a plan-stage audit: no Cargo.toml, Rust source, registry directory, or scripts/check.sh exists. No engine defect or green runtime verdict is claimed.

The architecture is an immutable REA journal on FrankenGraphDB, Folio as its write authority, Abacus/Almanac/Palimpsest for accounting laws, asynchronous certified register folds, Docket/Notary for provenance and outsider verification, Canon for deterministic intent evaluation, Lantern/Statements/Concordat for derived analysis, and Steward/Teller for governance and three shared surfaces.

The linked blockers preserve concrete counterexamples and source references. They are specification-repair tasks, not implementation-completion claims. The plan is not ready for major-1 schema freezing or implementation graph conversion until these contradictions are resolved consistently across normative appendices, prose, README, and AGENTS.

Validation performed: repository inventory; exact sixteen-ID invariant set; TOML toolchain pin parse; local foundation source tracing; arithmetic/calendar/hold counterexamples evaluated using Python exact integers and fractions; primary-source checks for Cargo source identity, transparency proof scope, TigerBeetle pending semantics, special fiscal periods, and incumbent GL corrections.

Do not close this issue merely because documentation changes. Require fresh review of all linked acceptance examples and the applicable future executable gates. No cargo test or repository-wide gate can currently run because their project inputs are absent.
notes: All thirteen linked blockers have plan repairs in ff3b6eb (see each bead's note for the section map). Per this bead's instruction, nothing is closed by CobaltGull; WhiteCreek is asked via Agent Mail thread fa-azu to re-review the acceptance examples and close or reopen each. Executable gates remain UNRUN until G0 lands scripts/check.sh and the registries.

title: Define control-record encoding and immutable lifecycle projections
description:
References: §§4.2, 5.10, 7.3, 8.3, 10.2, Appendix A/C/F (lines 286-317, 435, 483, 540, 606-620, 1144, 1200-1207, 1278-1279, 1329).
Every Entry requires 2 or more posting legs, including SchemaControl/PolicyControl/PeriodControl in the same EntryClass union. Creating the first chart/calendar/book or opening a Future period has no legitimate pair of posting legs. Encoding invented zero-value accounting legs would violate the no-prototype/no-fabricated-leg doctrine. Define a journal record union or a precisely class-dependent payload with control effects separate from posting legs.
Lifecycle objects are declared immutable after commit (FA-INV-02), yet Period.state is a versioned property, RestatementCase/CloseRun/Finding/DraftSet carry changing status, Capability carries revoked, and §5.10 compare-and-sets membership counters. Specify which immutable transition records are authoritative and which current-state objects are disposable projections, with reconstruction and known-at rules. Attestations on a Register must bind its coordinate/value digest rather than merely a mutable/rebuildable cell identity.
Negative examples: create an empty book and first account without fake legs; transition case Proposed→Approved→Posted without updating its original payload; rebuild lifecycle state from immutable transitions. W1-W4, G0.
Model follow-up: entity-scoped capabilities and cash-by-legal-entity registers require an authoritative entity assignment. Entry/Account/Leg schemas and declared edges do not identify an owning LegalEntity, and the Dimension kind list has no mandatory legal-entity dimension. Either constrain each book to one declared entity or specify the balanced entity dimension and membership checks; do not infer ownership from descriptions.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.1 immutability model (payload objects / lifecycle-by-transition objects with projected status / rebuildable projections); control classes carry legs=[] and a typed ControlPayload union (Appendix A); FA-INV-02 clauses payload-immutable, lifecycle-by-transition, control-record; LegalEntity.code and Book.entities with legal_entity as a mandatory balancing dimension (per-entity clause of FA-INV-01, §5.2); RegisterEquals binds cell_key + fold_digest (§9.4). Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: control records are live: PeriodControl (period transitions, CAS witness on the period state) and SchemaControl (chart install) carry legs=[] + ControlPayload; tests period_transition_is_a_control_record_with_no_legs_and_moves_the_state_mirror, control_records_round_trip. Class gating (WhiteCreek 2733): post admits only Original/Adjusting/Reversal; every other registered class refuses FA-REF-102 naming its bead; the admissibility note 'voids_expires' is NOT an executable predicate yet (Resolution refuses as not-implemented until fa-rqe).

title: Correct live foundation contracts for clocks, transactions, and dependency identity
description:
Baseline plan references: §§2.1, 5.10, 7.1/7.8, 18.4; Appendix H R-ST/R-SSI/R-VT (plan lines 82-86, 435, 475, 503, 1069, 1388-1391).
Observed against FrankenGraphDB HEAD b323bd17ceaf81e97ce89e43d8d9f6d5151695cf:
- crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs:3743 invokes marker_for_capsule on the durable write path; :5113 assigns commit_hlc = commit_seq. This is not a UTC HLC. Sequence snapshots exist, but AsOfTime, duration-from-recorded-time hold expiry, and claims that recorded instants already come from live markers are unsupported by this path.
- IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md:11 and :107-113 explicitly distinguish bounded WriteTxn/FCW from full SSI. Current write_txn_parts/point_reads.rs and vertex_scan_reads.rs do provide bounded read dependencies; the finding is not that all race protection is absent. The plan must name and prove the exact supported read/phantom/commit route, rather than claim full Block-MVCC + Graph-SSI is live and let plain WriteBatch reads imply transaction witnesses.
- fgdb/Cargo.toml:12 and fgdb-types/Cargo.toml:15 use git asupersync rev 78b64636..., while fastmcp_rust/Cargo.toml:42 uses crates.io =0.5.0. Plan version-only syntax does not unify those Cx identities. fgdb-prism/Cargo.toml:16-18 also uses git fnx rev 9d710b1c..., outside the proposed two-repository git allowlist. Direct registry fnx dependencies duplicate the source.
Required repair: exact source/rev/feature matrix and intentional root patches where necessary, no dependency weakening; explicit live UTC/time-evidence blocker and lawful interim absence; call-path-specific transaction probes including post/close, empty-range insertion, double application and limited-account races. Verify cargo metadata resolves one intended runtime and fnx identity per closure. Cargo reference: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/overriding-dependencies.html . This task spans W1/W2, first gate G0.

title: Reconcile CLI, schema, determinism, and public comparison contradictions
description:
References: §§0/3.2, 4.7, 9.4, 13.2, 15.3-15.7, 18.2/18.4, Appendix A/C/D; README examples/comparison.
- §4.7 and FA-REF-015 refuse instants as effective dates, while §15.3 silently converts with a warning. Pick one explicit policy. Period inadmissibility is exit 2 in Genesis but listed under exit 7 too.
- CLI fa hold is both financial hold and governance hold place/release; MCP catalog has no complete governance/registry/interop/lifecycle mapping despite parity claim. Declare unambiguous verbs and shared-operation mappings or registered exclusions.
- Closed/Locked matrix permits Resolution(Voids), Revision and Reopen, but §7.3/FA-INV-03 says only restatement classes; matrix requires post_softclosed, migrate, schema_change absent from the §14.2 closed op vocabulary. Reconcile from one registry.
- Bundles claim same scope+checkpoint yields same bytes but include producer, produced_at_seq, capability and redaction fields; bind the complete closure or split deterministic content from production receipt. Fixed-as_known_at RegisterEquals assertions cannot become false from later entries; use a separate head-following reconciliation monitor and retain the original assertion.
- §15.5 example needs IS edges, Subledger→Account CONTROLS, LegalEntity.code and Leg.effective_date not declared in the model. Fix the model/query contract and reject cross-unit sums in the accounting GQL profile.
- fa-formats/qbo and object_schemas/tracing/conversion laws need explicit registry ownership; ftui and fsci_stats are promised despite the closed four-foundation policy. Reconcile their inclusion/exclusion with explicit posture/test-only policy, never silent allowlist expansion.
- Plan/README characterize all ERP posted journals as editable rows. Oracle Fusion documentation explicitly says a posted journal cannot be changed and describes reversal workflows: https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/131/user_services/FAFTT/F416502AN10266.htm . Narrow competitive claims and separate existing derived balance caches from authoritative mutable accounting facts. SEC audit-trail amendments were adopted October 12, 2022, not 2023 as §0 says: https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2022-187 .
Acceptance: schema-backed examples, deterministic bundle repeat across callers/times under declared closure, immutable assertion vs head-monitor example, one exit per refusal, complete verb mappings, source-backed comparison language. W4/W5/W9, G0/G3.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: instants refused (FA-REF-015) never converted; exits reconciled (period inadmissibility = 7, accounting-law = 3; Genesis text fixed; dictionary a strict superset of fgdb's); Reserve/PostReserve/VoidReserve so fa hold is governance only; MCP clusters fa.book/chart/govern/io with a total verbs.toml mapping and two registered exclusions; §7.3/FA-INV-03 Locked wording; §14.2 closed ops list; ProductionReceipt split from the deterministic bundle body; immutable RegisterEquals + drift monitor; §15.5 example uses REPRESENTS/CONTROLS/LegalEntity.code/effective_day and per-unit sums; §18.2 registry ownership rows; ftui excluded from 1.0 and fsci_stats on a test-only allowlist; §0/§3.2 ERP claims narrowed; SEC date fixed. Left open for re-review.

title: Specify N-leg hold resolution, reserved availability, and expiry-period behavior
description:
References: §§5.4/5.5, 7.6, Appendix A/B/C/F/G (lines 409-415, 495, 1175, 1242, 1268, 1342, 1374).
Posts { amount: Amount } generalizes a two-leg TigerBeetle transfer inadequately to N-leg/multi-unit holds. A pending USD entry D A60, D B40, C cash100 resolved for 60 admits D A60/C cash60 or D A20/D B40/C cash60, both balanced and under original legs. Neither schema nor law chooses. Multiple currencies cannot fit one Amount. Require a per-leg balanced subvector, named proportional law, or explicit registered absence.
Limit reads say head net balance but do not define worst-case reserved availability. With cash100, a pending outflow80 must block a second80 and an unrelated posted outflow30; pending inflow cannot finance an outflow before resolution. Specify reserve/consume/release equations and atomic witnesses.
Pending created in Open can encounter Closed/Locked before timeout. Appendix C allows only Voids in Locked, excluding Expires; §5.4 requires Expires for every elapsed deadline, so the sweep can become permanently inadmissible. Define origin-vs-posting-period routing, unconditional lawful reservation release, and close/lock preconditions.
A bounded sweep cannot both expire every due hold in one transaction and obey max_batch_entries for an arbitrarily large due population. Pin epoch/cursor/batch progression and visibility under backlog. Apply the same precision to scheduled reversals after the target period closes.
Acceptance: the N-leg ambiguity above; multi-unit partial; pending-spend race; locked-period expiration; sweep batch overflow; crash/manual-resolution interleavings. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.4 Posts{posted_legs} per-leg balanced sub-vector (scalar = two-leg sugar; ProportionalPost law), resolution unique by identity-derived vid (manual void vs sweep = AlreadyLive conflict), timeout measured from the TimeEvidence tick, reserved-availability equations (pending outflows reserve, pending inflows never finance), SweepCursor batching under max_batch_entries; Appendix C Pending/Resolution rows (Voids/Expires admissible except Future); Appendix A Disposition; Appendix B PostReserve. Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: admissibility.toml encodes Resolution/Locked = admit with note voids_expires; the kernel does not yet evaluate dispositions (Resolution refuses FA-REF-102 until fa-rqe lands the two-phase reserve slice).

title: Close evidence-required and retention/erasure contract gaps
description:
References: §§8.5, 9.1/9.2/9.6, 10.2, 14.6, Appendix A/B/F (lines 548, 560-564, 580, 618, 795, 1152-1153, 1188-1194, 1232, 1254, 1332).
Common intent evidence is optional and Entry.evidence has no minimum or class-specific source contract. A registered Intent origin with an empty evidence list satisfies the written unknown-reference check vacuously, contrary to AGENTS' rule that an entry without registered evidence is unencodable. Define required real evidence by class (manual assertion/control authority may be explicit objects), and distinguish drafts from committable entries.
External documents retain locator+observed digest, not necessarily bytes. FA-INV-05 promises strong retention of the provenance closure for the retention floor. Specify durable custody requirements or a downgraded, non-equivalent external-evidence profile with failure behavior; a URL alone cannot ensure retention.
AttachEvidence appends edges after commit but Entry.evidence is digest-covered and immutable. Separate original posting evidence from later supplemental evidence, version the latter and specify how each closure is selected/certified.
Erasure promises no PII outside Party/Document, but immutable descriptions, leg memos, tags, external IDs, source-entered-by fields and structured event data can carry PII. Specify schema-level sensitive-field placement and key granularity; erasing a Party alone cannot remove those copies. Add live foundation ledger rows for erasure/retention/legal-hold capabilities rather than assuming them.
Acceptance: absent required evidence, lost external source, supplemental document after posting, PII in each allowed free-text location, legal hold vs erasure race, preservation of public amount commitments. W2/W4/Steward, G0.
Resolve provenance edge retention types too: bare substrate Oid/MarkerRef are identities, not retention edges. Appendix A imports a typed-reference law but uses bare Oids widely; enumerate strong/weak/cut-conditioned references and their erasure interaction so FA-INV-05 is actually enforceable.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §9.2 evidence_policy.toml minimums per class (ManualAssertion with reason code as the honest alternative; NeedsEvidence drafts cannot promote), external evidence retains bytes by default with an attested ByReferenceOnly downgrade, SupplementalEvidence as a new object; §8.5 Erasable<T> fields (description, memo, tags, external ids, migration names, event attributes) under per-Party subject keys, hold/erasure race as a witness conflict; Appendix A reference law (strong/weak/locator) and Erasable schema; Appendix H R-ERASE/R-RED/R-KEY; FA-INV-05 clauses. Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: Erasable review (WhiteCreek 2751/2756) accepted: deterministic sealing withdrawn before any commit; randomized salt+nonce from the facade's CryptoCx; AAD binds field_digest + subject_ref; retry equivalence = EntryPayload::semantic_digest under the key (in-memory normal form, never stored); FA-REF-033 when a sealed field cannot be opened; CLI intent_oid is a domain-separated BLAKE3 over (book, principal, key), never raw request bytes. Open question flagged to reviewers: proposal_digest covers full Erasable wire bytes (code) vs field_digest-only (prose).
2026-10-10 CobaltGull (WhiteCreek 2781 obligations, recorded): (1) authenticated requester binding must precede both the exact-digest and semantic retry paths — in the embedded posture the facade caller is the trusted process and proposal.principal_ref is its claim; the daemon/MCP posture must bind the principal from the session before calling post (lands with Steward, fa-llx); (2) the semantic transcript now carries each erasable field's subject_ref ahead of its plaintext, so distinct subject contexts never compare equal; (3) PostRequest no longer carries a separate principal_scope — identity scope is derived from proposal.principal_ref, and the base  capability is checked before any storage observation (doctrine 8). Remaining: caller-authenticated use is unsupported until Steward; documented on post().
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: correction — the previous note lost a word to shell expansion: it is the base "post" capability op that is checked before any storage observation.

title: Preserve publication and historical identity in migration and scenario interim postures
description:
References: §§5.8, 8.6, 15.2, Appendix G/H (lines 427, 552, 833-835, 1371, 1376, 1395, 1402).
§5.8 promises staging followed by one atomic migration finalization. R-BULK's interim is ordinary committed WriteBatch chunks with manifests/resume; no staging visibility or finalization filter is defined. Readers may see an incomplete migration, and a later bad chunk cannot roll back already committed entries. Specify durable staging within the same engine, activation semantics and failure/retry visibility, without deleting history.
Scenario fallback replays trunk into a fresh open_memory database, whose assigned CommitSeq/HLC and allocated VIds differ. Entry digests embed book/branch/account identities, and approvals/certificates bind those digests. Pin original-coordinate provenance and identity translation or a read-only base-plus-overlay abstraction so replay does not forge recorded time or claim original membership. Replaying only accounting objects cannot reproduce physical sequences containing access logs/checkpoints/maintenance.
Close rehearsal needs computable draft balances before substrate branches exist, but §15.2 describes draft materialization as future optional and scratch replay only for scenarios. State the shared law for all draft report reads and for promotion changing head.
Restatement case posting is atomic in §8.3/§5.1 yet Appendix G allows a separate case-transition transaction. Place the entries and posted-state effect in one transaction or specify exact recoverable state and idempotency preventing repost.
Acceptance: invalid final migration chunk, crash around activation; scratch replay with intervening system records; draft-to-trunk digest/approval changes; crash after case entries before transition. W2-W4/W5, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §8.6 MigrationRun staging invisible until Finalize (Abandoned runs stay journaled and invisible; retries are new runs); §15.2 one scratch-book law for drafts and scenarios (accounting objects only, identity-derived vids and seq-free payloads preserve digests and approvals, SeqMap in the certificate, no forged membership); Appendix G restatement case post is one write_ordered transaction with its LifecycleTransition. Left open for re-review.

title: Make unit evolution, signs, overflow, and FX residual laws mutually consistent
description:
References: §§4.4, 5.2, 6.1/6.4/6.7, Appendix A/F (lines 325, 395, 443, 455, 467, 1131-1132, 1145-1146, 1328, 1333).
1. Amount stores only unit_id and i128 mantissa. §4.4 allows changing that unit's scale and rescaling every stored mantissa, contradicting immutable entries and digests. Example: mantissa 100 means 1 at scale 2 and 0.1 at scale 3. Use immutable unit-version identity with a named conversion/migration law; never silently reinterpret or rewrite historical payloads. Distinguish precision changes from economic redenomination.
2. Entry legs have both Debit/Credit and signed i128 without a nonnegative-leg rule. Reversal wording says exact negation without deciding side swap vs signed storno. Negative legs can undermine per-side amount limits and produce two representations of the same posting. Define one canonical sign convention and boundary behavior, including i128::MIN.
3. Bounded checked i128 amounts are not an unrestricted ordered abelian group: MAX+1 and -MIN fail. Proofs/metamorphics need representability hypotheses or an unbounded reference domain; summation policy must define intermediate overflow and register cumulative totals.
4. FX residual encoding is incomplete: EUR debit 1 minor unit + debit 1 = credit 2; at rate 1/2 under HalfUp, USD base debits 1+1 != credit 1. Adding one USD credit residual fixes base balance but violates USD per-unit balance. Define lawful base-only valuation/residual effects or a complete balanced construction, including remeasurement and historical-cost release, without inventing funds or weakening FA-INV-01.
Acceptance must include these exact examples, inverse/cross-rate scale boundaries, negative refunds/allocations and both per-unit/base validation. W1/W2/W7, G0.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.4 immutable unit versions (USD@2 -> USD@4 via ScaleConversion law + Redenomination record; historical mantissas never reinterpreted), non-negative mantissas with side swap (no storno; i128::MIN unreachable), bounded register accumulators; §6.1 bounded abelian group with representability hypothesis and independent reference arithmetic; §5.2 valuation residual absorbed by a designated leg with the exact EUR 0.01+0.01/0.02 @ 1/2 HalfUp counterexample, conversion-account pairing for realized FX, revaluation through Valuation contra leaves; §6.5 lot laws. Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: fa-money valuation test realizes the EUR 0.01+0.01/0.02 @ ½ HalfUp counterexample (designated-leg residual). WhiteCreek 2744: per-legal-entity base equality + residual selection is NOT implemented; the kernel does no base valuation yet, so the single-residual Option is the single-entity subset; multi-entity proposals must refuse until the residual-list schema/checker lands (awaiting the fa-p7r handoff patch).

title: Specify public evidence commitments and scope-completeness proofs
description:
References: §§9.1/9.6, 11.11, 13.1-13.3, 15.6, Appendix A/F (lines 560, 580, 704, 745-755, 917, 1188-1194, 1217-1223, 1341).
The MMR is ordered by commit, whereas bundle scopes filter by effective period/account subtree, and retroactive entries make matching records noncontiguous. Inclusion proofs prove supplied leaves belong; they do not prove all matching leaves were supplied. Appendix A contains inclusion_paths but no range/selection-completeness proof, while the CPA workflow says fa-verify confirms a complete FY extract. A producer can omit one matching entry and all retained membership proofs still verify.
Define a sound supported proof mode (e.g. verify the full relevant prefix and selection or an authenticated predicate index bound to the same checkpoint), exact scope/known-at/auth intersection, missing-entry negative vectors, and accurate costs. Do not label membership_only as complete.
Document Oid uses the substrate's keyed identity (fgdb-crypto/src/lib.rs:80-97). A verifier with only public bundle/root cannot recompute it without K_oid. ImportReceipt.digest_at_receipt could provide a public binding, but its algorithm/domain and authenticated binding to Document Oid, kind, bytes and length are not specified. Require an explicit public body commitment chain without disclosing the storage key.
Whole-document hash alone also cannot verify arbitrary disclosed byte ranges against the original redacted document. Define chunk commitments or weaken the redaction proof scope honestly. Specify signature schemes, public trust anchors, key rotation and signed transcript; the std-only verifier budget must cover these implementations.
RFC scope reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html . W4/W9, G0/G1.
The canonical Entry deliberately excludes its creating MarkerRef/recorded time. An MMR leaf of only Entry bytes plus a checkpoint's aggregate commit_seq does not authenticate the per-entry commit sequence/HLC, especially when one commit has many leaves. Specify a domain-separated leaf envelope binding record kind, book/branch, creating marker/sequence, and within-commit ordinal, with canonical ordering and a proof of the sequence-to-prefix boundary used by historical selection.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §13.2 LeafEnvelope binding kind/coordinate/commit_seq/within-commit ordinal/selection fields; ScopeIndexComplete mode with scope_index_root in every checkpoint and boundary-neighbor proofs (missing-entry negative vectors); §9.1 public doc_commit over a 4 KiB chunk tree (substrate ObjectId is a locator only), redaction at chunk granularity labeled honestly; Ed25519 + TrustAnchorSet + KeyRotation in the std-only verifier budget; §13.1 completeness_scope labels; Appendix A LeafEnvelope/ScopeIndex/TransparencyCheckpoint/Bundle; FA-INV-14 clauses. Left open for re-review.

title: Remove approval and certificate hash cycles before freezing durable schemas
description:
References: §4.2/4.6, §10.1/10.4, Appendix A (plan lines 294-305, 333, 592, 645, 1128-1172, 1200-1223).
Entry BodyDigest excludes only entry_digest and includes approvals. ApprovalRef itself contains approved_digest. §4.6 requires that digest to equal the committed object's digest. Consequently d = H(entry containing approval.approved_digest = d), a cryptographic fixed point rather than a constructible approval flow. RestatementCase similarly embeds approvals and mutable lifecycle status. Attestation and checkpoint signature transcripts also lack explicit exclusions of the signatures and signed-digest fields.
Certificate/output references have a related missing contract: Finding contains certificate_oid and the certificate contains output_digest of the result; bundles contain report certificates; Origin::Intent contains plan_certificate_oid. Without a distinct semantic output body, hashing can become cyclic or depend on runtime IDs/approvals and make Canon's byte-for-byte replay claim impossible.
Required repair: an explicit acyclic identity/transcript graph separating immutable proposal digest, approvals/signatures, committed envelope digest, and certified semantic output. Bind approvals to complete effects, book, target coordinate and policy epoch; require reapproval if promotion replays materially different effects. Enumerate ordered construction and digest tags for every signed/certified type. Negative acceptance: change one leg after approval must fail, while adding the first valid approval must be constructible without finding a hash fixed point. W1/W3/W4, G0.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.6 acyclic identity graph (EntryProposal -> proposal_digest -> plan certificate -> Approvals binding proposal_digest+effects_digest+coordinate+policy epoch -> envelope entry_digest); Appendix A Entry/Approval/Attestation/Checkpoint transcripts exclude signatures/self-digests; normative construction order added; RestatementCase split into immutable body + projection with Approval objects; negative acceptance stated (leg change after approval => digest mismatch refusal; first approval needs no fixed point). Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: code consequences landed in fa-model/fa-journal: (1) plan_certificate_oid moved out of the proposal into the envelope (entry_digest = H(domain ‖ proposal_digest ‖ opt(plan_cert) ‖ approvals)); test envelope_fields_change_the_entry_digest_but_not_the_proposal_digest. (2) Idempotency: same key + different content refuses FA-REF-032 exit 6 on both the retry and race-recovery paths (RubyMoose 2739 / WhiteCreek 2730); tests identical_retry_is_recorded_and_a_changed_retry_is_a_conflict + CLI test. (3) Erasable sealing is deterministic under the key (salt/nonce KDF-derived) so identical retries compare equal; WhiteCreek carries the Appendix A row in their patch. (4) fa:entry:v1 is positional schema 1.0: the first additive field needs a minor bump + length-delimited extension block (WhiteCreek 2734) — not yet implemented; lands with the first schema patch that needs it.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: schema-review.patch (RubyMoose/WhiteCreek) APPLIED to the plan text; code parity, row by row — NOT YET ADMITTED by fa:entry:v1 as encoded: effective_date: Option<DateDay> (code: DateDay on every entry incl. controls); Disposition::Posts { source_ordinals } (code: posted_legs); settles.target_leg: EntryTarget (code: EntryRef); ControlPayload::ReservationRelease (absent); ProposalRef/EffectManifest/IntentOutcome objects (absent; no vid(IntentOutcome) yet, refusals are not durable); Certificate resolved_sequence/resolution_frontier/instant_resolution and DocumentStub proof grammar (no certificate/document code yet). ADMITTED: FA-INV-09 semantic-request equivalence (EntryPayload::semantic_digest, FA-REF-032/033). Each row lands with its slice via the minor-version + extension-block mechanism (msg 2734); the live codec is positional schema 1.0.

title: Bind commit authorization and audit delivery to explicit current policy
description:
References: §§5.1/5.10, 9.7, 14.2-14.4, Appendix A/G/H (lines 375-386, 435, 584, 779-787, 1224-1225, 1365-1375, 1399).
Plan has initial admission and commit-time SoD but no explicit current-policy witness for revocation/expiry between dry run and commit, or for reads pinned before revocation. known_at should select accounting history without resurrecting revoked access. Define security epoch, current authority evaluation, approval authority expiry/revocation policy and fail-closed boundaries.
daily_total and per-entry amount ceilings require a precise measure (gross debit, credit, absolute per-leg, per-unit), day/time-zone source, shared principal/token scope and serializable budget debit. Net of balanced entries is always zero. Attenuation/issuance must not reset a principal ceiling. No operation-cost row prices those stateful checks.
Every external-profile read must be completely logged, but Appendix G declares balance/report/bundle reads 0 writes. Define durable access recording before protected bytes escape, stream/cancellation/failure semantics, daemon authority for read-only callers, and avoidance of recursive log reads. Price the real transaction/barrier or name a distinct admitted audit path.
Account-subtree/dimension caveats and full immutable Entry payloads conflict when one entry crosses an authorized and unauthorized account: define whole-entry admission, redacted/partial-view representation and proof scope, or refuse before fetching; do not return the full other-account leg or silently describe a partial fold as whole-book.
Acceptance: revoke after plan, historical read using revoked token, two simultaneous daily-budget posts, token attenuation, crash before/after first protected output byte, and split-scope balanced entry. W2/Steward/W5, G0/G1.
The ordering of ADMIT→RESOLVE→CANON also needs explicit post-evaluation authorization: a typed event does not yet have its generated accounts/dimensions/amounts at step 1. Safely admit explicit inputs, run under restricted capabilities, then validate every generated effect and current caveat before commit. Initial authorization of the verb alone is insufficient.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.1 step 5 post-evaluation authorization of rule-generated legs; §14.2 closed ops vocabulary, current-policy witness at commit (PlanInvalidated{CapabilityRevoked}), historical selectors never resurrect authority, ceiling measure (per-leg mantissa; daily gross debits per root issuance; day from TimeEvidence) via a UsageCell, whole-entry visibility with partial_view; §9.7 AccessEvent committed before the first protected byte and priced as an Appendix G row; FA-INV-10 clauses. Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: capability checks in the Genesis slice are caller-supplied ops (Capability::with_ops) evaluated before observation for the base  op and inside the transaction for matrix ops; there is no authenticated principal binding yet (WhiteCreek 2781) — Steward (fa-llx) must bind principal + capability from an authenticated session before the kernel is reached, and the daemon must refuse caller-asserted principals.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: correction — the previous note lost a word to shell expansion: the base "post" op is checked before observation; matrix ops are checked inside the transaction.

title: Resolve special periods, carry-forward folds, and report cutoffs
description:
References: §§4.8, 7.1-7.5, 8.6, 12.1/12.5, 15.6, Appendix A/C/F (lines 349, 475-491, 552, 717, 733, 919, 1181, 1265-1279, 1330).
A date must resolve to exactly one Period, but normal December, adjustment period 13 and closing/opening periods can share civil dates. There is no target-period field on Entry/PostEntry or registered routing rule to disambiguate. Shared calendar identity also needs separation from per-book period state.
The fold boundary is not defined for stock vs flow: FOR PERIOD filters effective dates, while balance-sheet/TB positions require opening balances; §7.5 additionally posts next-year opening balances despite an all-time append-only fold. Simple cash 100 at year end plus a new opening 100 becomes 200 under All unless openings are anchors or an explicit selection law excludes double counting. Closing entries likewise must not zero the income-statement activity reported for the closed year.
§8.6 imports opening trial balance plus optional full legacy history; specify a cut so both cannot be counted twice.
§7.4 defines originally reported as first Closed, while close can include further adjusting entries before publication/lock. Either label this view as first close or persist a ReportPublication fact/certificate; retain AS REPORTED IN for actual filings.
Required examples: Dec 31 normal/adjustment/closing, FY aggregate, Jan opening, pre/post-close P&L and BS, known-at retrospective correction, multi-book shared calendar with independent status, migration opening+detail. Special-period reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ON-PREMISE/651d8af3ea974ad1a4d74449122c620e/2252d7531a4d424de10000000a174cb4.html . W1/W3/W7/W9, G0.
Appendix C refuses PriorPeriodAdjustment in Open/SoftClosed, although §8.1 defines it as an opening-retained-earnings adjustment. Decide whether it posts into the current open period while referring to historical error periods, or whether its class name means a different operation; do not force a current-period correction into a closed/locked target.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §7.3 effective_period discriminator (special periods must be named; class-restricted); §4.1 Period key per book with shared calendar; §7.5 stock-vs-flow rule (flow lines filter by period, stock lines fold EFFECTIVE <= end), income statements exclude Closing, no opening-balance entries, incremental reclose + nominal-zero; §8.6 migration-disjoint modes; §7.4/§12.5 AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED anchored to StatementIssuance; Appendix C PriorPeriodAdjustment row posts in the current open period with relates_to.
